encoding.decision_index: Includes inline conditions, short-circuit Boolean operators, comparisons, comprehensions, loop controls and exceptions; node is the ast.walk ordinal
encoding.required_field: No class-body default; dataclass inheritance/factories may change the effective constructor default
encoding.defaults: Declarations and factories, not live environment values; see validation and profile methods in program
encoding.authority: program is exact implementation semantics; descriptions are source docstrings and may contain historical wording
encoding.exceptions: Explicit handlers/raises are indexed; implicit Python and dependency exceptions remain governed by Python and dependency semantics
encoding.resources: Verbatim local JS, configuration and template sources; no JS control-flow analysis is claimed

        CREATE TABLE visible_ids AS

modules.description: Configuration models for WarpBuster Core.

symbols.description: Named threshold profiles selected from normalized activity semantics.

Named thresholds for local physical-transition analysis.

Attributes:
    profile: Stable name of the threshold profile.
    absolute_impossible_speed_mps: Absolute human-movement ceiling in metres
        per second. ``None`` disables speed-only impossible classification for
        activity types without a justified physical ceiling.
    absolute_impossible_distance_m: Minimum transition distance in metres needed
        to classify an excessive apparent speed as physically impossible.
    relative_suspicious_speed_floor_mps: Conservative lower bound in metres per
        second for any baseline-relative suspicion.
    relative_speed_multiplier: Multiplier applied to the median local speed.
    relative_mad_multiplier: Multiplier applied to median absolute deviation and
        added to the median local speed.
    relative_suspicious_distance_m: Minimum transition distance in metres needed
        for baseline-relative suspicion.
    minimum_baseline_samples: Minimum positive-time transitions needed before
        median/MAD evidence may raise the suspicious speed floor.
    island_search_max_elapsed_seconds: Maximum elapsed time in seconds searched
        forward from an impossible entry transition.
    island_search_max_exit_candidates: Maximum later impossible transitions tested
        as exits for one entry, bounding worst-case search work.
    bridge_max_speed_mps: Maximum direct trusted-anchor speed in metres per second
        that can support a plausible bridge. ``None`` disables island detection.
    bridge_speed_floor_mps: Minimum derived bridge limit in metres per second.
    bridge_baseline_multiplier: Multiplier applied to median local speed when
        deriving the bridge limit.
    diagnostic_max_candidate_details: Maximum bridge candidate details retained
        for reports; aggregate counters are never truncated.
    one_sided_search_max_records: Maximum records inspected after an unpaired
        impossible transition when looking for missing-exit cluster evidence.
    one_sided_max_clean_gap_records: Maximum records without new suspicious or
        missing-position evidence that may join evidence into one cluster.
    one_sided_anchor_min_normal_transitions: Consecutive NORMAL transitions
        required outside each proposed one-sided cluster boundary.
    one_sided_anchor_scan_max_records: Maximum records inspected outward from
        either proposed trusted anchor.
    one_sided_max_diagnostics: Maximum candidate diagnostics retained; aggregate
        counters are never truncated.
    tail_anchor_min_normal_transitions: Consecutive adjacent NORMAL transitions
        required before a tail entry and for reachable recovery (count); default 15.
    tail_position_error_budget_m: Combined anchor/observation position uncertainty
        added to the physical reachability radius, in metres; default 50.
    vertical_warning_speed_mps: Sustained absolute vertical speed in metres per
        second that merits a sensor-consistency warning. ``None`` disables the
        scan for activity types without a justified profile.
    vertical_warning_single_transition_speed_mps: Higher absolute vertical speed
        that can create a warning from one transition.
    vertical_warning_min_delta_m: Minimum absolute altitude change per transition.
    vertical_warning_min_consecutive_transitions: Consecutive lower-threshold
        transitions required for a sustained warning.
    vertical_warning_max_count: Maximum warnings retained in a report.
    geometry_min_chord_distance_m: Minimum endpoint distance in metres for a
        near-collinear geometry warning.
    geometry_min_position_count: Minimum positioned observations in a warning.
    geometry_max_cross_track_deviation_m: Maximum perpendicular deviation in
        metres from the candidate chord.
    geometry_max_path_to_chord_ratio: Maximum sampled-path/chord ratio.
    geometry_scan_max_window_records: Maximum positioned observations inspected
        by one bounded candidate window.
    geometry_scan_stride_records: Number of positioned observations between
        candidate window starts.
    geometry_max_bearing_change_degrees: Maximum chord-bearing difference in
        degrees when merging overlapping candidate windows.
    geometry_max_warnings: Maximum warnings retained in a report; aggregate
        diagnostics still count omitted warnings.
    distance_spike_*: Conservative, bounded proof for an impossible cumulative
        distance step corroborated by a complete speed stream and conflicting
        position displacement. Units are metres, seconds, ratios and records.

Point acceptance policy, separate from physical corruption detection.

Named thresholds and bounds for GPX course reconstruction.

These values affect only optional reconstruction after integrity detection.
They are deliberately separate from ``IntegrityConfig``.

Active local matching uses ``anchor_match_tolerance_m`` (metres),
``anchor_candidate_deduplication_m`` (course chainage metres) and
``ambiguity_score_margin_m`` (metres). Context requires 15 NORMAL transitions;
endpoint gaps additionally require 30 observations. The per-side 300-record /
300-second caps bound that search. At most 128 full path allocations are tried
per gap across all context windows; truncation is never called unique.

Local observed progression uses qualified recorded-distance deltas or preserved
GPS geometry. The context error budget is observed_length * ratio + the two
measured projection errors, with every intermediate point within anchor tolerance.
Gap signal consistency allows the larger of the relative tolerance and
``signal_distance_absolute_tolerance_m``: a small absolute budget for short
paths, not an expansion of the GPS edit scope or the anchor match radius.
The ``missing_completion_*`` speed and record-count bounds now cover all gaps.

Deprecated compatibility fields, not used by the local planner:
``one_sided_anchor_*``, ``one_sided_drift_*``,
``signal_course_length_ratio_*`` and ``anchor_stability_scan_max_records``.
They remain readable for old callers/config dumps, not as write-scope controls.
``mixed_region_*`` still configure standalone diagnostic grouping in safety.py;
diagnostic envelopes never grant permission to edit coordinates.
Reject unsafe or contradictory reconstruction bounds.
Operational bounds for advisory OSM candidate discovery only.
Conservative 2D application gates; never used by Integrity Detector.
Approximate forest-path application; units match the confirmed allocator.
Coarse, provider-neutral thresholds for advisory path ranking.

'Named thresholds and bounds for GPX course reconstruction.

    These values affect only optional reconstruction after integrity detection.
    They are deliberately separate from ``IntegrityConfig``.

    Active local matching uses ``anchor_match_tolerance_m`` (metres),
    ``anchor_candidate_deduplication_m`` (course chainage metres) and
    ``ambiguity_score_margin_m`` (metres). Context requires 15 NORMAL transitions;
    endpoint gaps additionally require 30 observations. The per-side 300-record /
    300-second caps bound that search. At most 128 full path allocations are tried
    per gap across all context windows; truncation is never called unique.

    Local observed progression uses qualified recorded-distance deltas or preserved
    GPS geometry. The context error budget is observed_length * ratio + the two
    measured projection errors, with every intermediate point within anchor tolerance.
    Gap signal consistency allows the larger of the relative tolerance and
    ``signal_distance_absolute_tolerance_m``: a small absolute budget for short
    paths, not an expansion of the GPS edit scope or the anchor match radius.
    The ``missing_completion_*`` speed and record-count bounds now cover all gaps.

    Deprecated compatibility fields, not used by the local planner:
    ``one_sided_anchor_*``, ``one_sided_drift_*``,
    ``signal_course_length_ratio_*`` and ``anchor_stability_scan_max_records``.
    They remain readable for old callers/config dumps, not as write-scope controls.
    ``mixed_region_*`` still configure standalone diagnostic grouping in safety.py;
    diagnostic envelopes never grant permission to edit coordinates.
    '

[build-system]
requires = ["setuptools>=75"]
build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"

[project]
name = "warpbuster"
dynamic = ["version"]
description = "Detect and repair physically impossible GNSS data in FIT activities"
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.14"
authors = [
    { name = "WarpBuster contributors" },
]
classifiers = [
    "Development Status :: 3 - Alpha",
    "Environment :: Console",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.14",
    "Typing :: Typed",
]
dependencies = [
    "fitdecode>=0.11,<0.12",
]

[project.urls]
Repository = "https://github.com/zloynemec/warpbuster"

[project.optional-dependencies]
osm = [
    "warpbuster-osm-manager==0.1.0.dev0",
    "warpbuster-osm-routing==0.1.0.dev0",
]
dev = [
    "garmin-fit-sdk>=21.214,<22",
    "mypy>=1.13,<2",
    "pytest>=8.3,<9",
    "ruff>=0.8,<1",
]

[project.scripts]
warpbuster = "warpbuster.cli:main"

[tool.setuptools.dynamic]
version = { attr = "warpbuster.__version__" }

[tool.setuptools.packages.find]
where = ["src"]

[tool.setuptools.package-data]
warpbuster = ["py.typed", "report/assets/*.html"]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
addopts = "--strict-config --strict-markers"
markers = [
    "integration: offline integration tests that may require an optional local runtime",
    "private: tests that require ignored private activity files",
]
testpaths = ["tests"]

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 100
target-version = "py314"

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["B", "E4", "E7", "E9", "F", "I", "RUF", "SIM", "UP"]

[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.14"
strict = true
warn_unused_configs = true

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = ["fitdecode"]
ignore_missing_imports = true

# WarpBuster OSM Manager configuration.
# Copy this file to ./osm-manager.toml; it will be loaded automatically.
# Use --config only to select a different file explicitly.

[osm_manager]
# Local, location-sensitive cache. Use an absolute path in unattended environments.
cache_directory = "/replace/with/platform/cache/path"

# OSM acquisition identity and endpoint. HTTPS is mandatory.
overpass_url = "https://overpass-api.de/api/interpreter"
user_agent = "warpbuster-osm-manager/0.1 (+https://github.com/zloynemec/warpbuster)"

# Coverage planning.
gpx_corridor_buffer_m = 1000.0
cache_grid_zoom = 12
coverage_sample_cell_fraction = 0.5
default_max_age_seconds = 2592000

# Geographic and request fan-out limits.
maximum_requested_area_km2 = 2000.0
maximum_ensure_cells = 512
maximum_cells_per_overpass_request = 32
maximum_overpass_requests = 128

# Network and response limits.
maximum_download_bytes = 268435456
maximum_ensure_download_bytes = 536870912
network_timeout_seconds = 180.0
maximum_retry_count = 2
retry_backoff_seconds = 1.0
retry_jitter_seconds = 0.25
http_read_chunk_bytes = 65536

# Cache writer coordination.
cache_lock_timeout_seconds = 60.0
stale_lock_seconds = 900.0
lock_poll_seconds = 0.1

# Local input and validation limits.
maximum_input_file_bytes = 33554432
maximum_import_bytes = 2147483648
maximum_gpx_points = 1000000
maximum_gpx_segment_length_m = 100000.0
maximum_gpx_total_length_m = 5000000.0
maximum_osm_objects = 5000000

# Garbage collection only removes unreferenced blobs older than this age.
prune_minimum_age_seconds = 86400

# WarpBuster Task 010B derived Valhalla graph cache.
# CLI --cache-dir overrides this value; WARPBUSTER_OSM_ROUTING_CACHE_DIR is used
# when neither CLI nor TOML specifies a directory.
[osm_routing]
cache_directory = "/absolute/path/to/osm-routing-cache"

# Immutable OSM Manager manifest and source ceilings.
maximum_manifest_bytes = 1048576
maximum_data_files = 64
maximum_total_source_bytes = 2147483648

# Streaming OSM normalization ceilings.
maximum_osm_objects = 5000000
maximum_total_node_references = 50000000
maximum_total_tag_bytes = 536870912
maximum_diagnostic_items = 100
maximum_output_pbf_bytes = 2147483648

# Derived Valhalla artifact ceilings.
maximum_tile_files = 250000
maximum_total_tile_bytes = 8589934592
build_timeout_seconds = 900.0

# Per-graph filesystem lock behavior.
cache_lock_timeout_seconds = 60.0
stale_lock_seconds = 1800.0
lock_poll_seconds = 0.1

# Hashing and conservative cache pruning.
io_chunk_bytes = 1048576
prune_minimum_age_seconds = 604800.0

# Task 010D audited request policy. These values do not affect graph identity.
snap_search_radius_m = 100.0
maximum_snap_distance_m = 30.0
equivalent_snap_separation_m = 3.0
snap_ambiguity_distance_delta_m = 10.0
maximum_snap_candidates = 64
maximum_reported_candidate_groups = 8
route_endpoint_tolerance_m = 5.0
maximum_route_distance_m = 250000.0
maximum_route_shape_points = 16000
maximum_route_edges = 16000
route_length_absolute_tolerance_m = 10.0
route_length_relative_tolerance = 0.01

# Task 010E request-time alternatives policy; no graph rebuild is required.
# Additional paths, excluding primary. CLI defaults to 0; runtime supports at most 2.
maximum_requested_alternates = 2
# Shared UTF-8 byte budget for route, traces and fallback metadata responses.
# Checked before parsing; not a C++ memory cap.
maximum_alternatives_response_bytes = 8388608
# Total decoded route/trace/metadata points and edges, including duplicates and failed attempts.
maximum_total_route_shape_points = 48000
maximum_total_route_edges = 48000
# Advisory only: diversity BELOW this ratio warns, but never removes a unique route.
minimum_diversity_ratio = 0.10
# Advisory only: candidate/primary length ABOVE this ratio warns, never filters.
detour_warning_ratio = 1.50

# Task 010G narrow single-edge direction recovery, no graph rebuild required.
# Additional trace attempts per route: 0 disables fallback, 1 permits one map_snap.
maximum_trace_fallback_attempts_per_route = 1
# Batched metadata requests per route (two route endpoints): 0 or 1.
maximum_trace_metadata_queries_per_route = 1
# Metres, graph endpoint projection only; route/trace sequences must match EXACTLY.
trace_edge_projection_tolerance_m = 0.25
# Fraction of edge; trace reports 3 decimal places, locate reports 5.
trace_percent_along_tolerance = 0.001

# Task 010H: optional approach sequence, start ambiguity only. 0 disables.
context_snapping_enabled = 1
# Records / seconds / metres; match Core collection limits when customizing.
context_maximum_points = 60
context_maximum_age_s = 60.0
context_maximum_length_m = 150.0
context_maximum_step_s = 5.0
context_minimum_points = 8
context_minimum_duration_s = 7.0
context_minimum_progress_m = 10.0
# Metres: absolute errors, total backward chainage and advantage over each rival.
context_maximum_median_error_m = 20.0
context_maximum_p90_error_m = 25.0
context_maximum_backtrack_m = 3.0
context_minimum_margin_m = 10.0
# Fraction of points supporting the winner, across full and recent windows.
context_minimum_support_ratio = 0.8
context_recent_points = 5
# Total local work across competitors. No additional locate calls.
context_maximum_groups = 8
context_maximum_vertices = 4096
context_maximum_projection_work = 245760
# Metres: near-equal local minima at distinct chainages refuse.
context_projection_tie_m = 0.25

# Task 010I: approximate candidate discovery; no graph rebuild required.
# Enabled per RouteAlternativesRequest; Core discovery opts in.
approximate_snap_distance_m = 100.0       # maximum anchor connector, metres
approximate_projection_merge_m = 20.0    # local projection chainage separation, metres
approximate_maximum_groups = 2           # road groups per anchor
approximate_maximum_pairs = 4            # native routing requests per gap
approximate_minimum_context_support = 0.6 # usable projection fraction for advisory ranking

FROM python:3.14.7-slim-trixie AS builder

ENV PIP_DISABLE_PIP_VERSION_CHECK=1 \
    PIP_NO_CACHE_DIR=1

WORKDIR /build

COPY pyproject.toml README.md ./
COPY src ./src
COPY packages/osm-manager ./packages/osm-manager
COPY packages/osm-routing ./packages/osm-routing
COPY web/pyproject.toml ./web/pyproject.toml
COPY web/backend ./web/backend

RUN python -m pip wheel --wheel-dir /wheels \
      pyvalhalla==3.8.3 osmium==4.3.0 \
      . ./packages/osm-manager ./packages/osm-routing ./web


FROM python:3.14.7-slim-trixie AS runtime

ARG APP_UID=10001
ARG APP_GID=10001

ENV PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 \
    PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 \
    PIP_DISABLE_PIP_VERSION_CHECK=1 \
    WARPBUSTER_WEB_DATA=/data \
    WARPBUSTER_WEB_STATIC=/app/web/dist \
    WARPBUSTER_WEB_OSM_MODE=auto \
    WARPBUSTER_WEB_PORT=8080

LABEL org.opencontainers.image.title="WarpBuster Web" \
      org.opencontainers.image.source="https://github.com/zloynemec/warpbuster"

RUN apt-get update \
    && apt-get install --yes --no-install-recommends libexpat1 \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* \
    && groupadd --gid "${APP_GID}" warpbuster \
    && useradd --uid "${APP_UID}" --gid "${APP_GID}" --no-create-home --shell /usr/sbin/nologin warpbuster \
    && install -d -o "${APP_UID}" -g "${APP_GID}" -m 0700 /data /app/web

COPY --from=builder /wheels /wheels
RUN python -m pip install --no-index --find-links=/wheels warpbuster-web==0.1.0 \
    && rm -rf /wheels

COPY --chown=${APP_UID}:${APP_GID} web/dist /app/web/dist

USER ${APP_UID}:${APP_GID}
WORKDIR /app

EXPOSE 8080

HEALTHCHECK --interval=20s --timeout=4s --start-period=15s --retries=3 \
    CMD ["python", "-m", "warpbuster_web.healthcheck"]

CMD ["python", "-m", "warpbuster_web", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "8080"]

WarpBuster activity report

Track geometry

Original / preserved Reconstructed Candidate Course Corrupted Skipped Missing data OSM candidate

Interactive OpenStreetMap: drag to pan, use +/− or the mouse wheel to zoom, and toggle layers in the top-right control. In repair output, grey lines are preserved coordinates and blue lines are reconstructed coordinates including joins. Dashed orange bridges mark unknown geometry, not a recovered path. Kilometre labels use FIT distance; distance uncertainty is shown in the summary and marker popups. G-numbers identify gaps, not the spans between kilometre labels.

Local gap reconstruction

G-numbers identify reconstruction gaps, not corrupted detector regions. Click a row to inspect its local path. Course start/finish are assumptions authorized by --fill-missing-from-course; preserved observations are not snapped to the course.

OSM reconstruction candidates

Discovery lists possible routes; the application status identifies the selected path. Search is non-exhaustive. An automatically selected route is an approximate hypothesis, not a confirmed travelled path.

Automatic repair decisions

Accepted GPX first, then OSM by score, full length and route ID. Failed candidates allow the next alternative.

Selection and rejected attempts

    


    

      
Best path candidate

      

      

      
The recommendation compares discovered GPX and OSM paths. It is advisory and is not applied to the FIT file.

    


    

      
Numbered input detector regions

      
A number identifies a display region, not its severity. The GPX course is a reference overlay only and is excluded from integrity detection. MISSING does not mean CORRUPTED. A visually unusual unnumbered FIT section may simply lack sufficient course-independent evidence.

FIT-only inputs and observed GPS

      

      

      
Coverage measures usable original GPS over active time before reconstruction. A supplied point is an assumed place at the activity boundary, not a timed FIT observation. Approximate paths may differ from the route actually taken.

    


    

      
Missing-position completion

      

      
Reconstruction fills original missing or independently invalidated coordinates. Preserved GPS observations, timestamps and recorded telemetry remain unchanged. Demonstrably impossible distance increments can be corrected locally; plausible distance is not replaced merely to match the course.

    


    

      
Composite GNSS regions

      

      
Components are classified without the reference course. A diagnostic region may contain proven-corrupted, tainted, plausible, unknown and missing data; inclusion in the region alone does not authorize coordinate changes.
